parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the work done by a force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A block of mass $m$ is raised vertically at constant speed. The vertical height gained by the block is $\Delta h$, as shown in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

Fig. 3.1

Derive an expression, in terms of $m$ and $\Delta h$, for the change in gravitational potential energy $\Delta E_{\text{P}}$ of the block. State the meaning of any other symbols you use.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: An electric motor has an input power of $900 \text{ W}$. The motor takes $1.0$ minute to lift a load of weight $240 \text{ N}$ at constant speed through a vertical height of $150 \text{ m}$. Resistive forces are negligible.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Show that the work done by the motor on the load in $1.0$ minute is $36 \text{ kJ}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the useful output power of the motor.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (c)(ii) to determine the efficiency of the motor.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text:
Some of the power wasted in the motor is dissipated by the resistance of its coil. This dissipated power is $280 \text{ W}$.

The coil of the motor is made from wire of total length $23 \text{ m}$. The wire has a cross-sectional area of $2.6 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}^2$ and is made from metal of resistivity $1.7 \times 10^{-8} \Omega \text{ m}$.

Calculate the current in the coil.
